text.p: The chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, has entered a Sarajevo hospital for five days of medical treatment, a government official said on Thursday.

Izetbegovic, 71, who suffered heart problems last February, was admitted to the Kosevo hospital heart clinic as part of scheduled treatment and his life was not in danger, spokesman Mirza Hajric told Reuters.
Doctors wanted to check on Izetbegovic's condition nearly a year after he suffered a heart attack while he was serving as Bosnian president, Hajric said.
He spent some three weeks in hospital last year and later received treatment at home.
The Sarajevo-based BH press agency quoted the head of Izetbegovic's office as saying that the president would continue to perform his duties during the five-day hospital stay.

After leading the country through a 3-1/2 year war of independence against separatist Serb forces, Izetbegovic was elected in September as the Moslem member of a three-man presidency ruling over Serb and Moslem-Croat territories.
